title.value: Updates of Equilibrium Prop Match Gradients of Backprop Through Time in an RNN with Static Input
title.justification: The title is clearly stated at the beginning of the provided paper excerpt.
title.quote: Updates of Equilibrium Prop Match Gradients of Backprop Through Time in an RNN with Static Input

analysis.description: The paper presents a discrete-time version of Equilibrium Propagation (EP), an algorithm inspired by biological processes for training recurrent neural networks (RNNs) with static inputs. This version simplifies computations and reduces the time required for simulation, making it more practical for machine learning tasks. The authors demonstrate both theoretically and empirically that the updates of EP match the gradients of Backpropagation Through Time (BPTT) under certain conditions. The paper also introduces a convolutional architecture trained with EP that achieves approximately 1% test error on the MNIST dataset, which is the best result reported for EP.

type.justification: The paper involves theoretical demonstration as well as numerical experiments, indicating it is empirical as it applies and tests the concepts on actual data.
type.quote: We numerically demonstrate the GDU property on a small network, on fully connected layered and convolutional architectures.

name.justification: The paper primarily deals with training methods for recurrent neural networks (RNNs) with static input using the Equilibrium Propagation approach.
name.quote: Equilibrium Propagation (EP) is a biologically inspired learning algorithm for convergent recurrent neural networks, i.e. RNNs that are fed by a static input x and settle to a steady state.

name.justification: The paper discusses and compares the Equilibrium Propagation with Backpropagation Through Time (BPTT) as one of the main algorithms.
name.quote: We first prove theoretically, as well as numerically that the neural and weight updates of EP, computed by forward-time dynamics, are step-by-step equal to the ones obtained by BPTT, with gradients computed backward in time.

name.justification: The paper introduces a convolutional architecture trained using Equilibrium Propagation and reports results on it.
name.quote: This allows us training the first convolutional architecture with EP, reaching ∼ 1% test error on MNIST, which is the lowest test error reported with EP.

name.justification: The model, Equilibrium Propagation (EP), is central to the paper as an alternative to traditional backpropagation methods for training RNNs.
name.quote: Equilibrium Propagation (EP) is a biologically inspired learning algorithm for convergent recurrent neural networks, i.e. RNNs that are fed by a static input x and settle to a steady state.

is_contributed.justification: EP is not claimed as a new contribution; rather, the paper presents a discrete-time formulation of an existing EP framework.
is_contributed.quote: Originally, EP was introduced in the context of real-time leaky integrate neuronal dynamics [Scellier and Bengio, 2017, 2019]. In this paper, we propose a discrete-time formulation of EP.
